transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55 minutes | Recording: Yes
Attendees: Ben Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neil (AstraMed CTO), Rachel Ng (Head of Infra), Samir Patel (Security)

Summary (auto): Align on networking pattern for Redwood Private POC, confirm region and egress restrictions, agree benchmarks and timeline.

[00:00] Ben Carter: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ben from redwood. quick roll call?
[00:10] Liam O'Neil: liam here.
[00:12] Rachel Ng: rachel here.
[00:13] Samir Patel: samir on security.
[00:15] Maya Singh: maya here, im the se who'll run the bench with you.
[00:20] Ben Carter: quick agenda: data residency, networking options (vpc peering vs privatelink), egress constraints, bench targets and timeline for a 4 week poc. sound good?
[00:30] Liam: yes, that's right. high level — we need to keep PHI in region and we can't have uncontrolled egress to the internet, ok?
[00:40] Samir: yep, plus customer-managed KMS and audit logs, SOC2 artifacts, and we need proof of zero-knowledge handling for prompts with PHI.
[00:50] Maya: understood, we've done this with other health customers; we support private deployments that sit in your vpc and we can do vpc peering or aws privatelink depending on your networking posture.
[01:10] Rachel: side note — we prefer not to open cross-account ingress broadly; peering requires route table changes which our network team is sensitive about. privatelink tended to be easier in our org for service-to-service.
[01:30] Ben: fair. for the POC we usually spin up Redwood Private in your account as a managed control plane, or we can run an on-prem package — for you frankly given PHI i'd recommend Redwood Private in your AWS account with CMK.
[01:50] Liam: we wanted the control plane in our account, yes. can you confirm region support for us-east-1? most of our data needs to remain in virginia.
[02:05] Maya: yes, we can deploy the control plane and serving nodes in us-east-1. if you need eu-west-1 we can mirror regionally but that is an extra step.
[02:20] Samir: do you support customer-managed KMS (CMK) for at-rest model cache and any logs?
[02:28] Maya: yes, CMK supported. note that some ephemeral tokens and IPC might require short-lived service creds but we can lock down access to the required roles.
[02:40] Ben: ok let's go into success criteria — liam, what would you consider a win for this poc?
[02:50] Liam: three things: 1) latency — p95 < 250ms for our 256-token LLM flows, 2) throughput — sustain 30 qps with minimal tail latency, 3) quality parity with our existing hosted baseline (we'll have a reference testset). security/compliance checkboxes must be green.
[03:14] Maya: good, that's actionable. we'll run an initial baseline with 100 concurrent connections and 256 token context; our bench harness will produce p50/p95/p99 and trace logs.
[03:30] Rachel: what's the expected resource sizing for that load? GPUs, instance types?
[03:36] Maya: for a Llama-2-ish 13B style model quantized to int8, you'd need a single V100-class equivalence to get those numbers at moderate concurrency; for preferred production-like results we recommend at least 2x A10/A100 equiv to hit consistent 30 qps with headroom. i'll put exact vm sku and cpu/memory in the runbook.
[03:58] Ben: note — some of that is model dependent. if you want lower latency we can try a trimmed model variant or compilation knobs. cost vs latency tradeoff.
[04:10] Samir: about egress — we cannot allow outbound traffic to internet except to our monitoring endpoints and aws kms. can you guarantee no egress to third-party telemetry?
[04:20] Maya: yes, by default the deployment can be configured with no external egress; metrics can be pushed to your prometheus or we use a pushgateway inside your network. we don't require external telemetry.
[04:35] Liam: ok, how do you handle model updates and patching if the control plane is in our account?
[04:42] Ben: updates are controlled by you — we provide an operator and can do canary rollouts inside your infra. for the poc we'll agree on a version and freeze during benchmarks.
[04:55] Rachel: are we peering with a redwood account or is it all in our account?
[05:00] Maya: recommended pattern: deploy serving nodes in your account (Redwood Private inside customer account) so there's no cross-account egress except optional PrivateLink control plane calls. If you'd rather not grant subnet attachments we can use PrivateLink and keep control plane in Redwood but that requires a PrivateLink endpoint in your VPC.
[05:20] Samir: PrivateLink sounds safer from an audit viewpoint. Peering changes are sensitive.
[05:25] Ben: ok we'll note PrivateLink as preferred for AstraMed for the POC.
[05:30] Rachel: for data residency — we must ensure logs with PHI are not stored off region. can you redact PII in audit logs?
[05:40] Maya: we can configure redaction rules and never persist raw prompts to long-term logs; short-lived traces for debugging can be masked and stored only in-region. we'll document retention policy.
[05:52] Liam: how will you measure parity for quality? we have a testset of 200 prompts and expected responses. we need to be able to run the same prompts in the POC and compare diffs.
[06:05] Maya: perfect — send the testset and we'll run automated scoring (BLEU-ish/embedding-based similarity) and provide a report.
[06:12] Ben: timeline proposal: Week 0 (networking & account setup), Week 1 (deploy & baseline), Week 2 (scale bench), Week 3 (tweaks & re-run), Week 4 (evaluation & decision). total 4 weeks.
[06:30] Rachel: that works. we can dedicate a network engineer for week 0.
[06:35] Samir: security review — we'll need SOC2 docs and architecture diagram for our infosec review.
[06:42] Ben: i'll send SOC2 summary and architecture by 3/18 as action.
[06:46] Maya: also, for bench we'll need a narrow ping window (2-4 hours) where we run load from your env to the serving nodes. this avoids noisy neighbors.
[06:58] Liam: good, we'll schedule that in week 2.
[07:03] Rachel: can you also confirm firewall ports and inbound rules required for PrivateLink?
[07:09] Maya: yes, PrivateLink typically needs the ENI and the endpoint service; we'll provide exact ports (443 for TLS api, and a few ephemeral ports for management if you allow). we'll provide a limited list.
[07:22] Ben: on benchmarks — specifics: target payloads are 256-token inputs, average response ~80 tokens; we'll run synthetic latencies and also an internal replay of a day of traffic but scaled down. target sustained 30 qps, spike to 60 qps for short bursts.
[07:40] Maya: agreed. we'll instrument p95 and p99. also we'll capture token cost and RU numbers per request so you can estimate unit economics.
[07:50] Samir: does the POC include encryption in transit with mTLS between services?
[07:56] Maya: yes, within the VPC we can do mTLS; for PrivateLink endpoint it's TLS and you can put an internal ALB with mTLS if you require mutual auth.
[08:06] Liam: one more — network egress to s3 for model artifacts, can that be limited to our s3 endpoints only?
[08:15] Maya: yep, we can restrict s3 access to your buckets and limit to VPC endpoint or S3 VPC gateway endpoints.
[08:22] Ben: ok i want to capture the success criteria exactly so no confusion: p95 latency <250ms on 256 token prompts; sustain 30 qps for 1 hour without errors; quality parity >= 95% on your testset embedding similarity; security: CMK in-region, redaction enabled, no public egress. agreed?
[08:45] Liam: yes agreed.
[08:47] Rachel: agree.
[08:49] Samir: agree pending SOC2 docs.
[08:52] Ben: excellent. quick risks: if you insist on single AZ only we might see higher latencies on failover; recommend cross-AZ patches. also model size may push cost up — we'll show options.
[09:05] Maya: i'll include a recommended instance profile: 2x A10/80gb GPUs equivalent + n replicas for headroom; also provide a small config for cheaper perf tests.
[09:16] Liam: what's the estimated cost for the 4 week POC? rough ballpark so we can secure approval.
[09:22] Ben: rough estimate: infra ~ $6-10k depending on GPU SKUs for test period; Redwood services and engineering support we'll itemize in the SOW. i'll give a tighter estimate in the SOW doc.
[09:36] Rachel: ok deliverables we need from redwood before week 0: network checklist, endpoint IPs/privatelink instructions, SOW draft, benchmark harness.
[09:46] Ben: noted. we'll deliver by 3/18.
[09:50] Maya: i'll follow up to schedule the week 0 call and the week 2 benchmark window.
[09:55] Liam: thanks all. one last Q from me — will logs ever leave region for analytics?
[10:02] Maya: not unless you opt-in; we can keep analytics in-region and push metrics to your datadog/prometheus inside the account.
[10:10] Ben: ok wrap up — recap action items, send docs, schedule week 0. thanks everyone.
[10:20] Rachel: thanks.
[10:22] Samir: thanks.
